svg.aria-label: Key events first: the motion of a thrown crate with its key events, one coarse token per event, the fine blocks between key frames in four segments, and the block-causal attention mask across the two levels
svg.text: 1. The motion of a thrown crate, and the moments its regime changes (a sketch in closed form, not data)
height of the crate (0 to 1.1 m)
its speed (0 to 5 m/s): it jumps at the events
2. The coarse pass, generated first: one token per key event, with the object's state at that frame
3. The fine pass, one segment at a time: the step-wise regressor runs from one key frame to the next
block by block as before, but every block also reads the key frame its segment must reach and the event there; a speed error
stops at the next key frame instead of travelling to 3 s; segments start at known key frames, so they are independent and run in parallel
Training: one pass trains both levels. The key frames come from the recorded motion (the event
extractor on the engine's contacts). The fine pass reads them teacher-forced; a share of them are
corrupted on purpose (shifted by a block, moved, dropped or invented), so it learns to reach an
imperfect key frame instead of trusting it.
Generation: coarse pass first, from the scene and the action alone; then every segment, in parallel.
Risk: a wrong coarse pass cannot be repaired below it. A missed collision gives a smooth motion with
no collision; a key frame 20 cm off is reached exactly. So the fine pass is scored with recorded and
with predicted key frames separately, and the coarse pass as an event detector (precision, recall,
timing), not only through the final motion.
block-causal across levels: a row reads its filled columns;
fine slots read the coarse tokens, never the reverse
